analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It changes docs/provider/quickstart.md (head lines 62-71, 105-116) and docs/reference/configuration.md (head patch lines 180-186), and no executable code was supplied. The changes describe Autopilot, which can now download catalog builds on the operator's behalf once consent is saved. The downloads are controlled by a new `[backend.autopilot_downloads]` section with enabled, max_storage_gb, max_models and reserve_gb keys. A new owner-only ledger file, autopilot-downloads.json, records the downloads. Scheduled windows keep cached Autopilot builds whose bytes hash unchanged.

Security-relevant observations, all from documentation text and none verified against implementation:
- Downloads default to enabled once consent exists, and the max_storage_gb and max_models caps default to none. The documented reserve_gb default is 50 GiB, and the doc says nothing is deleted. Disk-fill exposure (T-016) is therefore operator-influenced and bounded by that reserve. This is a design choice documented transparently, not a regression.
- The model-weight integrity concern (A-004, T-012, T-027) depends on the implementation re-verifying catalog builds and hashes when they are added to the set. The docs say "verified catalog build" and "bytes hash unchanged", but the Swift sources (AutopilotStartInventory, ProviderLoop+AutopilotModelSet, AutopilotDownload*) were not supplied. A later pass should confirm that downloads use the pinned CDN with hash verification and that the ledger cannot add unverified builds.
- The ledger autopilot-downloads.json is claimed to be owner-only from creation, capped at 256 entries, and to keep builds in the set when the catalog is unreachable. A reviewer should check that persisted ledger entries are re-hashed before use, so a local operator editing the ledger cannot inject unverified models (T-012 is operator-adversarial anyway).
- Autopilot is shadow-only per the docs, so there is no change to attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011) or the coordinator wire contract.
- The pinned links and the "latest default branch" wording are consistent with the canonical rescope. No new endpoints are introduced.

No findings qualify. needs_deeper_review is set to true only because the implementation claims could not be checked from the supplied evidence.
